class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class
end
# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
# request for it, are shared too.
class Citation < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi

  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment

  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }

  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
  def request_enrichment
    with_lock do
      if enrichment_pending?
        false
      else
        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
        true
      end
    end
  end

  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
  def enrich
    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
  rescue Provider::Error => error
    fail_enrichment(error.message)
  end

  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
  end

  private
    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    def record_enrichment(attributes)
      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    end
end
# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
class Export < ApplicationRecord
  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def cancellable?
    queued? || working?
  end

  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
  def cancel
    with_lock do
      if cancellable?
        update!(status: :cancelled)
      else
        false
      end
    end
  end

  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
  # keeps no file.
  def generate
    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    return unless start(notes.size)

    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
      fragments << markdown_for(note)
      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    end

    finish(fragments.sum)
  end

  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
  def downloadable?
    completed? && expires_at.future?
  end

  private
    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    def start(total)
      with_lock do
        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
      end
    end

    def record_progress(count)
      with_lock do
        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
      end
    end

    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    # export always has one.
    def finish(markdown)
      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")

      completed = with_lock do
        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
      end

      blob.purge unless completed
    end

    def markdown_for(note)
      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
      markdown
    end
end
require "csv"

# A CSV of notes for one notebook. A preview reads and validates the rows without
# saving anything. Applying validates them again and saves the import with every
# row's note, or saves nothing.
class Import < ApplicationRecord
  HEADERS = %w[ title body_html doi annotation reminder_epoch ]
  MAXIMUM_SIZE = 100.kilobytes
  MAXIMUM_ROWS = 100

  Row = Struct.new(:line, :note, :annotation)

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_many :notes, dependent: :nullify

  validate :csv_is_importable, on: :create

  # Reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to reject a larger file.
  def file=(upload)
    self.csv = String.new(upload.read(MAXIMUM_SIZE + 1).to_s, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  def csv
    @csv.to_s
  end

  def csv=(text)
    @csv = text.to_s
    @rows = nil
  end

  def rows
    parse unless @rows
    @rows
  end

  # The reader's annotations by source line.
  def annotations
    rows.each_with_object(ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess.new) do |row, annotations|
      annotations[row.line] = row.annotation
    end
  end

  # Validates the file and every row without saving. Returns whether the import
  # can be applied, leaving the errors on the import and each row's note.
  def preview
    valid? && rows.map { |row| row.note.valid? }.all?
  end

  def apply
    return false if invalid?

    transaction do
      save!
      rows.each do |row|
        return false unless row.note.save
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def receipt
    CSV.generate do |csv|
      csv << %w[ title doi ]
      notes.includes(:citation).order(:id).each do |note|
        citation = note.citation
        csv << [ note.title, citation && citation[:id] ]
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def parse
      @rows, @headers, @problem = [], nil, nil
      return if csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE || !csv.valid_encoding?

      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))
      citations = {}
      next_line = 1

      reader.each do |fields|
        line, next_line = next_line, next_line + reader.line.count("\n")

        if @headers.nil?
          @headers = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
          break if @headers != HEADERS
        elsif fields.size != HEADERS.size && fields.any?
          @problem = "line #{line} has #{fields.size} fields instead of #{HEADERS.size}"
          break
        elsif fields.any?
          @rows << build_row(line, fields, citations)
          break if @rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        end
      end
    rescue CSV::MalformedCSVError => error
      @problem = "it is not valid CSV (#{error.message})"
    end

    # Rows naming the same DOI share one citation, so it is created only once.
    def build_row(line, fields, citations)
      title, body_html, doi, annotation, reminder_epoch = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
      citation = citations[doi] ||= Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?

      note = Note.new(notebook: notebook, import: self, title: title, body: body_html, citation: citation,
        annotation: annotation.presence, reminder_epoch: reminder_epoch.presence)

      Row.new(line, note, annotation.presence)
    end

    def csv_is_importable
      rows

      if csv.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, :blank)
      elsif csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE
        errors.add(:csv, "must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_SIZE)} or smaller")
      elsif !csv.valid_encoding?
        errors.add(:csv, "must be UTF-8 text")
      elsif @problem
        errors.add(:csv, "cannot be read because #{@problem}")
      elsif @headers != HEADERS
        errors.add(:csv, "must start with the header row #{HEADERS.join(",")}")
      elsif rows.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain at least one note")
      elsif rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain #{MAXIMUM_ROWS} notes or fewer")
      end
    end
end
class Note < ApplicationRecord
  HIGHLIGHT_COLORS = %w[ yellow green blue pink ]
  MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE = 1.megabyte

  belongs_to :notebook
  belongs_to :import, optional: true
  belongs_to :citation, optional: true, foreign_key: :citation_doi, validate: true
  has_rich_text :body

  enum status: { draft: 0, ready: 1 }, _prefix: true

  serialize :tags, JSON
  store_accessor :settings, :color
  alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :color, inclusion: { in: HIGHLIGHT_COLORS }, allow_blank: true
  validates :reminder_epoch, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0, less_than: 10_000_000_000 }, allow_nil: true
  validate :attachments_are_small

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :titled_like, ->(query) { where("notes.title ILIKE ?", "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%") }

  def doi
    citation_doi
  end

  # Cites the shared citation with this exact DOI, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
  # A blank DOI removes the citation from the note.
  def doi=(doi)
    doi = doi.to_s.strip
    self.citation = (Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?)
  end

  # The reminder time in the reader's time zone.
  def reminder_at
    Time.find_zone!(notebook.user.time_zone).at(reminder_epoch) if reminder_epoch
  end

  # Twenty-four elapsed hours after the reminder time, for postponing it a day.
  # The result keeps the reminder's UTC offset, so across a daylight saving
  # change its wall-clock time differs from the reader's local time.
  def next_day_reminder_at
    reminder_at.to_time + 86_400
  end

  def reminder_scheduled?
    reminder_job_id.present? && reminder_sent_at.nil?
  end

  # Schedules an email reminder at the given time in seconds since 1970, by
  # default the stored one, such as an imported reminder. It replaces any
  # earlier reminder for this note: the earlier job sends nothing when it runs.
  # Returns whether the reminder was scheduled. The job is queued under the row
  # lock, so a failed enqueue leaves the previous reminder in place.
  def schedule_reminder(epoch = reminder_epoch)
    with_lock do
      self.reminder_epoch = epoch

      if reminder_epoch && valid?
        job = NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch).perform_later(self)
        update!(reminder_job_id: job.job_id, reminder_sent_at: nil)
      else

# The configured citation metadata service. It answers GET /works?doi=... with a
# JSON title and source URL, using HTTP basic authentication. Settings come from
# config/secrets.yml, which reads them from the environment.
class Citation::Provider
  # The provider answered, but cannot supply metadata for this DOI.
  class Error < StandardError; end

  # The provider cannot answer now. Asking again later may succeed.
  class Unavailable < StandardError; end

  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)

  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
  end

  def lookup(doi)
    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?

    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)

    case response.status
    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    end
  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error
    raise Unavailable, "The provider could not be reached (#{error.message})"
  end

  private
    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    def connection
      Faraday.new(url: @url, request: { open_timeout: 2, timeout: 5 }) do |faraday|
        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]
        faraday.request :basic_auth, @user, @password
      end
    end

    def metadata_from(body)
      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)

      if title.is_a?(String) && title.present? && web_url?(source_url)
        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)
      else
        raise Error, "The provider's response did not include a title and web address"
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise Error, "The provider's response was not valid JSON"
    end

    def web_url?(url)
      uri = URI.parse(url.to_s)
      uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      false
    end
end

def within_new_transaction(isolation: nil, joinable: true)
        @connection.lock.synchronize do
          transaction = begin_transaction(isolation: isolation, joinable: joinable)
          ret = yield
          completed = true
          ret
        rescue Exception => error
          if transaction
            transaction.state.invalidate! if error.is_a? ActiveRecord::TransactionRollbackError
            rollback_transaction
            after_failure_actions(transaction, error)
          end

          raise
        ensure
          if transaction
            if error
              # @connection still holds an open or invalid transaction, so we must not
              # put it back in the pool for reuse.
              @connection.throw_away! unless transaction.state.rolledback?
            elsif Thread.current.status == "aborting" || (!completed && transaction.written)
              # The transaction is still open but the block returned earlier.
              #
              # The block could return early because of a timeout or because the thread is aborting,
              # so we are rolling back to make sure the timeout didn't caused the transaction to be
              # committed incompletely.
              rollback_transaction
            else
              begin
                commit_transaction
              rescue Exception
                rollback_transaction(transaction) unless transaction.state.completed?
                raise
              end
            end

        end

content.text:
# Rails 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0: upgrade risk report for Margin Notes

The upgrade has four high-risk changes. Each one changes behaviour without raising an error: imports can save partially, digests cover a different day, retries break in a way that leaves citations stuck at "pending", and jobs can fail while old and new versions run side by side. There are also two medium and seven low changes. I only read the gem source, changelogs and app code; I didn't install or run anything.

I unpacked Rails 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 in `/tmp/gems/{7.0.8.7,8.1.0}` to compare them, and the 7.1.0, 7.2.0, 8.0.0 and 8.1.0 changelogs are in `/tmp/gems/cl/`. The re-resolved lockfile is `/tmp/lock/Gemfile.lock`. Changelog links below are of the form `https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v<version>/<component>/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Facts about the app that the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)
- **Database:** PostgreSQL only (`config/database.yml`). All MySQL and SQLite changes are ruled out.
- **Defaults:** `config.load_defaults 7.0` (`config/application.rb:10`). I assumed it stays at 7.0. Raising it adds the further risks listed at the end.
- **Background jobs:** Active Job runs on Sidekiq 6.5.12 with redis 4.8.1 (`config/application.rb:24`). Tests use the `:test` adapter. `ExportJob` is a plain Sidekiq job that doesn't go through Active Job.
- **Rendering:** the app renders HTML with Turbo, importmap, Sprockets and Action Text. It loads its own Trix 1.3.5 from `vendor/javascript/trix-1.3.5.js`. Active Storage uses the local disk.
- **Cache:** none outside development, where it's the memory store. Cache-store changes are not relevant.
- **Other gems that move (from the re-resolved lockfile):** rack stays on 2.x because Sidekiq 6.5 pins it. New or changed gems are bigdecimal 4.1.3, json 3.1.0, rack-session, rackup, webrick, useragent, action_text-trix, securerandom and uri. Ruby 3.3.6, pg 1.6.0, concurrent-ruby 1.3.4 and minitest 5.x all still resolve.

## High risk

**1. An early `return` inside `transaction` now commits instead of rolling back.**
- **Before:** in 7.0, `within_new_transaction` rolled back when the block exited early after writing (code I read).
- **Now:** 7.1 added `commit_transaction_on_non_local_return`, 7.2 removed the rollback behaviour, and 8.0 removed the setting. In 8.1 an early exit always commits (code I read).
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:53-56`. The block calls `save!` on the import, then does `return false unless row.note.save` for each row.
- **What could go wrong:** if a row fails validation, the import record and every row saved before it are committed. That is a partial import, and it contradicts "saves nothing".
- **Tests:** the test "invalid rows ... saves nothing" (`test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:48`) should catch the commit (my inference).
- **Fix:** `raise ActiveRecord::Rollback`, or validate the rows before opening the transaction.
- **Source:** activerecord CHANGELOG v7.1.0 (around line 318) and v7.2.0 ("Remove deprecated behavior that would rollback a transaction block when exited using return...").

**2. Time arguments to Active Job now keep their time zone, which changes which day a digest covers.**
- **Before:** the 7.0 `TimeWithZoneSerializer` deserialised in the worker's `Time.zone`, which is UTC (code I read).
- **Now:** 8.1 also serialises `time_zone` and deserialises in that zone (code I read; activejob CHANGELOG v7.2.0, "Preserve the serialized timezone...").
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/user.rb:41` passes `requested_at` in the reader's zone.
  - `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day`.
- **What could go wrong:** the digest now covers the reader's local day rather than the UTC day. The subject date and the list of notes change for readers who are not on UTC. It also no longer matches the reservation key built from the UTC day in `user.rb:36`.
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:5-37` encodes the old behaviour and should fail (my inference).
- **Decision needed:** choose between local day and UTC day. If you keep UTC, convert explicitly in the mailer.

**3. `retry_on ... wait: :exponentially_longer` no longer works, and it fails only when a retry happens.**
- **What changed:** the option was deprecated in 7.1 and removed in 7.2 (activejob changelogs). In 8.1, `determine_delay` raises `"Couldn't determine a delay based on :exponentially_longer"` (code I read).
- **Where:** `app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`.
- **Why it's easy to miss:** the app boots normally and the error appears only when the provider is unavailable.
- **What could go wrong:** the RuntimeError escapes to Sidekiq's own retries, so `fail_enrichment` never runs. The citation stays `pending` forever, and `request_enrichment` then refuses every new request (my inference).
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:60` should catch it.
- **Fix:** `:polynomially_longer` gives the same timing.

**4. Big decimals in job arguments use a new format, which breaks old and new versions running side by side.**
- **What changed:** 7.1 added `BigDecimalSerializer` behind an opt-in, and 7.2 made it the only format (activejob CHANGELOG v7.1.0 "Fix BigDecimal (de)serialization", v7.2.0 "Remove deprecated primitive serializer").
- **Where:** `DigestJob.perform_later(..., reading_completion)` in `app/models/user.rb:41` passes a BigDecimal.
- **What could go wrong:** during a rolling deploy, a 7.0 Sidekiq worker can't deserialise a job queued by 8.1, so the job fails and goes into retries. The other direction is fine: `BigDecimal(params[:completion])` in `digest_mailer.rb:10` accepts both a String and a BigDecimal (my inference).
- **Mitigation:** drain the queue or deploy the workers first.
- **Also checked:** scheduled `NoteReminderJob` payloads from 7.0 deserialise fine in 8.1 (my inference).

## Medium risk

**5. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed (deprecated in 7.1, removed in 7.2).**
- **Source:** railties changelogs.
- **Where:** `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`, which reads `config/secrets.yml`.
- **What breaks:** a NoMethodError, but only when an enrichment job runs, not at boot.
- **Decision needed:** there is no direct replacement. Move the settings to credentials, `config_for(:citation_provider)`, or plain ENV.
- **Tests:** `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:40` covers it.

**6. The built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated in 8.1 and will be removed in 8.2.**
- **Source:** activejob CHANGELOG v8.1.0. `check_adapter` emits the warning (code I read).
- **Where:** `config/application.rb:24`, with sidekiq pinned at 6.5.12.
- **Decision needed before 8.2:** Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later moves to redis-client.
- **Code that will need review then** (my inference):
  - `Sidekiq.redis { redis.sadd(...) }` in `app/models/user.rb`, whose boolean return value would change.
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` in `app/models/notebook.rb`.

## Low risk

These all raise errors that booting the app or running the tests would catch.
- **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`app/models/note.rb:12`): a positional coder raises ArgumentError since 7.2. Use `coder: JSON`.
- **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`note.rb:10`): keyword syntax was removed in 8.0. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true`.
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`note.rb:14`): `color` comes from a `store_accessor` and is not a real attribute, so 8.1 raises ArgumentError (code I read). Use `alias_method` for both the reader and the writer.
- **`citation[:id]`** (`app/models/import.rb:68`): Citation's primary key is `doi`. In 8.1, `[:id]` no longer maps to it and raises MissingAttributeError (code I read; activerecord v7.1.0 deprecation, v7.2.0 removal). The receipt CSV would return a 500 error. Use `citation.doi`. The receipt test at line 6 should catch it.
- **`NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)`** (`note.rb:61`) passes an Integer. 8.1 stores it as-is and then calls `scheduled_at.utc.iso8601` while serialising the job, which raises NoMethodError (code I read). Use `Time.at(reminder_epoch)`. `reminders_controller_test.rb` covers it.
- **`fragments.sum`** (`app/models/export.rb:42`): Active Support's string-friendly `sum` override was removed in 7.1, so Ruby raises TypeError. It has been deprecated since 7.0. Use `join`. `test/models/export_test.rb` should catch it.
- **`ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags += ...`** (`config/initializers/action_text.rb`): since 7.1 the default is nil, so this raises NoMethodError at boot (actiontext CHANGELOG v7.1.0). Base the list on `sanitizer_allowed_tags`.
- **`show_exceptions = false`** (`config/environments/test.rb:31`): boolean values were removed in 7.2. 8.1 treats `false` like `:all`, so exceptions are rendered as error pages instead of raised (code I read). The `assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)` tests in exports and notes would fail. Use `:none`.
- **`has_secure_password` (since 7.1):** passwords longer than 72 bytes now fail validation instead of being silently truncated (my inference from Active Model 7.1).

## Not relevant, or only if `load_defaults` is raised
- **Database adapters other than PostgreSQL, multi-database, and encryption:** not used.
- **Cache-store changes:** the app uses no cache store outside development.
- **Action Cable and Action Mailbox:** stubs only.
- **`config.active_record.postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`:** enabled only by `load_defaults 7.2`. If you adopt it, `Date.iso8601(day)` in `app/models/notebook.rb:40` will raise, because `select_rows` will return Date objects.
- **`default_column_serializer = nil`:** enabled by `load_defaults 7.1`. If you adopt it, `serialize :preferences` in `notebook.rb:7` will raise.
- **HTML5 sanitizer:** also enabled by `load_defaults 7.1`. It changes how Action Text output is sanitised.
- **`to_time` keeping the zone (8.0 and 8.1):** `note.rb:44` only uses the epoch through `.to_i`, so results don't change. The comment there becomes inaccurate (my inference).
- **`ActiveRecord::Base.connection` soft deprecation** (`notebook.rb:40`): no warning by default.
- **Trix moved into the `action_text-trix` gem (8.1):** the app loads its own Trix 1.3.5 alongside the 8.1 `actiontext.js`. I didn't check whether they are compatible; check the editor in a browser.
- **json 3.1.0 and bigdecimal 4.1.3 arrive as new transitive dependencies:** I didn't review their changes. The relevant code is `JSON.parse` in `app/models/citation/provider.rb` and the BigDecimal division in `User#reading_completion`.
